newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: James Joyce gets Irish budget handout.
newsitem.headline: James Joyce gets Irish budget handout.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn on Wednesday unveiled a tax-cutting budget which he said would benefit everyone -- including the dead writer James Joyce.

Quinn said that since 1997 was the 75th anniversary of the publication of "Ulysses", one of the writers' most celebrated works, he would give the James Joyce Centre in Dublin 100,000 punts ($161,700).
This sum would, he said, "secure the future of this literary heritage centre for generations to come".
The grant was part of a package which included the first cut in standard rate of income tax -- from 26 to 25 percent -- in five years.
Every year Dubliners dress up in Edwardian clothes to mark Bloomsday, named after the central character in "Ulysses".

Opposition Progressive Democrat Michael Mcdowell charged that Quinn's budget had frittered away the nation's wealth and said this year's Joyce festivities should be called "Gloomsday, not Bloomsday". ($1=.6186 Punt)
